title: Enterprise Sales Kit: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview:

This enterprise sales kit consolidates Redwood Inference positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance for common buyer scenarios, two concise case studies, and a security FAQ tailored for prospect conversations. Use this as a one-stop reference for SDRs, AEs, and Solutions Engineers when preparing enterprise conversations or proposals.

1) Executive positioning and messaging

Short elevator (30 seconds):
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical in production by combining a high-performance serving runtime, unified control plane, and flexible deployment modes (hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/VPC).

Key value props (talking points):
- Production-first performance: predictable latency and throughput with GPU-optimized runtime and smart batching to meet SLAs for customer-facing applications.
- Control over economics: transparent per-token/embedding pricing, reserved capacity contracts, and tooling (batching, caching, quantization) to lower unit cost.
- Deployment flexibility: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated or isolated workloads.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: smart routing, model fallbacks, and observability that keep features live under load or partial failures.

Differentiated evidence (brief):
- Verified performance profiles across curated open models; customer benchmarks typically show 20-40% lower tail latency vs unmanaged endpoints in our target workloads.
- Rollout primitives (canary, A/B, automatic fallback) and token-level cost/latency dashboards used by platform teams for risk-managed rollouts.

Target personas and pain points:
- Product/ML engineers: need stable, low-latency inference and versioned model rollouts.
- Platform/Infra teams: require predictable capacity, observability, and cost controls.
- Security/compliance teams: need private deployment, KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs.

2) Short competitive brief (win themes vs common competitors)

Competitor: Large cloud AI platform (managed endpoints)
- Typical buyer concerns: vendor lock-in, variable unit economics, limited model customization.
- Redwood win themes: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private + clear cost controls and model variant fallbacks for reliability.

Competitor: LLM API provider focused on simplicity
- Typical buyer concerns: scale & enterprise features (SLA, private deploy), cost at scale.
- Redwood win themes: production-grade SLOs, reserved capacity, and observability for debugging regressions at scale.

Competitor: Self-hosted inference runtime vendors
- Typical buyer concerns: operational burden and slow internal iteration velocity.
- Redwood win themes: managed hosted or dedicated offerings with optional private deployments and tooling that reduce ops lift compared to DIY.

Competitive rebuttals (scripted bullets):
- When buyer claims they can self-host for cheaper: ask about engineering hours for runtime tuning, scaling KV cache, and ongoing kernel/hardware optimization - incremental ops cost is often higher than reserved capacity.
- When buyer mentions a cloud provider: emphasize cross-environment consistency and enterprise controls (private control plane + KMS/HSM) that cloud-native endpoints may not match without significant engineering.

3) Recommended pitch deck (10-12 slides - slide guidance and speaker notes)

Slide 1 - Title & hook:
- Company, logo, one-line value prop: "Predictable, economical LLM inference for production."

Slide 2 - The problem:
- Latency variability, unbounded token costs, rollout risk, and compliance barriers for regulated workloads (examples: chat product tail latency, monthly inference spend unpredictability).

Slide 3 - Our solution (how Redwood solves it):
- Runtime + orchestration + obs. Call out hosted/dedicated/private as three clear paths.

Slide 4 - How it works (high-level architecture):
- Serving runtime (GPU-optimized), smart routing, caching & batching, and deployment abstraction. Include a simple diagram: client -> routing -> runtime pool (hosted / dedicated / private) -> model catalog.

Slide 5 - Performance & cost controls:
- Tailored batching, quantization profiles, and token-level dashboards. Example metric: 95th percentile latency target for Dedicated and typical cost reduction ranges.

Slide 6 - Reliability & rollouts:
- Canary/A-B, automatic fallback, and tracing hooks for quick triage.

Slide 7 - Security & compliance:
- Private deployments, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SOC2 and ISO alignment (see security FAQ slides).

Slide 8 - Pricing overview & example scenarios:
- High-level tiers: Hosted (usage-based), Dedicated (reserved capacity), Private (license + support). Show two example TCO scenarios (see next section).

Slide 9 - Case studies (two short wins):
- SaaS company A: reduced latency by 35% and 42% cost per 1M tokens using reserved capacity + caching.
- Marketplace B: switched to private deployment to meet data residency and reduced incidents with automatic fallbacks.

Slide 10 - Implementation & timeline:
- Proof-of-concept (2-4 weeks), pilot (4-8 weeks), GA rollout (quarterly cadence). Roles: Solutions Engineer, Customer SRE, and Account Exec.

Slide 11 - Pricing & contracting next steps:
- How to request dedicated capacity sizing, example SOW items, and procurement checklist.

Slide 12 - Appendix & security FAQ pointer:
- Link to detailed security FAQ and deployment checklist.

4) Pricing guidance & example scenarios

Pricing primitives (how to talk about them):
- Hosted API: usage-based billing (per-token for generation, per-embedding for vector ops).
- Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput and SLAs; usually combined with minimum commit.
- Private: enterprise licensing for private control plane or on-prem package; usually license + support + optional onboarding.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, premium SLAs, compliance evidence packages.

Example pricing language (do not quote exact public list prices in early prospecting; obtain latest pricing sheet):
- "For a high-volume chat use case, customers commonly start with dedicated reserved capacity to stabilize latency and then apply batching and caching recommendations to reduce unit cost. In typical pilots we see 20-50% cost improvement vs unmanaged endpoints, depending on model and prompt profile."

TCO example scenarios (illustrative only):
- Scenario A - Consumer chat startup (10M tokens/month): Hosted is easiest for POC; projected 3-4 month runway on credits. If volume grows predictably, recommend Dedicated sizing (e.g., 1-2 GPU nodes reserved) to lower per-token.
- Scenario B - Regulated fintech (sensitive data): Recommend Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) + KMS integration and annual license; include onboarding and SOC2 evidence pack in contract.

Contracting tips:
- For Dedicated deals, negotiate monthly/annual commit with clear overage rules and a migration path between Dedicated and Private if needed.
- Include success milestones in SOW (POC acceptance criteria: latency threshold, throughput target, quality gate).

5) Case studies (short vignettes for prospect conversations)

Case study 1 - "SaaS Assist" (B2B SaaS company)
- Problem: Token costs spiked during user growth and tail latency caused degraded UX during peak hours.
- Solution: Dedicated reserved capacity + KV prefix caching + quantization profile.
- Outcome: 35% reduction in 95th percentile latency, 42% lower cost per 1M tokens.
- Timeline: POC (3 weeks), pilot (6 weeks), full rollout (3 months).

Case study 2 - "Global Marketplace" (two-region deployment)
- Problem: Data residency requirements and intermittent model-serving outages with their prior provider.
- Solution: Private deployment (VPC), cross-region routing with automatic fallback to compatible model variants, enterprise support.
- Outcome: Compliance requirements satisfied, 2x reduction in incident MTTR due to tracing hooks and canary rollouts.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers to common questions)

Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Hosted customers can choose region-aware storage; default retention window is documented in the contract and can be shortened per enterprise policy. Private deployments keep all data within the customer VPC/on-prem environment.

Q: Do you have SOC2/ISO certifications and can you provide evidence?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II alignment and has ISO-27001 alignment artifacts available for enterprise customers; we provide evidence packages during procurement under an NDA.

Q: How is encryption handled in transit and at rest?
A: All network traffic uses TLS 1.2+/modern ciphers. Data at rest in hosted infrastructure is encrypted using industry-standard AES-256. For private deployments customers can integrate their KMS/HSM.

Q: Can we use customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM?
A: Yes - Private deployments and select Dedicated customers can integrate with their KMS/HSM for key management. Hosted customers have managed KMS options and an upgrade path to CMK for enterprise contracts.

Q: How do you support data residency and sovereignty requirements?
A: We offer region selection for hosted deployments, Dedicated capacity in specific cloud regions, and private/VPC or on-prem packaging for strict data residency needs. We maintain a documented data residency checklist for each customer engagement.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities exist?
A: Token-level cost/duration logs, request tracing, and audit logs for admin actions are available. For private deployments, logs can be forwarded to the customer's logging endpoint. Retention windows and audit export formats are configurable via contract.

Q: How do you limit model exfiltration / PII leakage risk?
A: We recommend prompt/eval guardrails, content filters, and private deployment options. We also provide quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and regression alerts to detect unusual model outputs.

Q: What is the incident response process and SLA?
A: We provide incident response playbooks, a published SLA for Dedicated customers (uptime targets and latency goals), and on-call escalation paths for enterprise customers. Detailed incident response procedures are provided in the contract annex.

7) Enablement assets & next steps

Must-have collateral to attach to outbound or AE outreach:
- One-page positioning PDF (one-liner + 3 bullets + customer quote).
- 10-slide pitch deck template (editable).
- Security FAQ PDF and compliance evidence checklist (NDA required for full artifacts).
- Pricing worksheet and Dedicated sizing template for Solutions Engineers.
- Two longer-form case studies (customer-approved quotes).

Common next steps for AE/SE after first call:
1. Send one-page positioning doc and tailored pitch deck.
2. Schedule technical follow-up (Solutions Engineer) with pilot acceptance criteria.
3. Share security FAQ and request NDAs for compliance artifacts if needed.
4. Provide preliminary Dedicated sizing and pricing worksheet.
